title: Update the claimed CORE test firmware
scope: Supervised CORE firmware installation for the permanent-identity handshake.
preconditions: The operator is authorized, the registry record is claimed and provisioned, and the verified original public key is available.
Only the selected CORE is connected. The old application is running and supports the reviewed P1 proof.
The new role-specific application image is qualified, guarded and locally available. Retain local evidence before installing.

steps.action: Select the claimed CORE and confirm only it is connected.
steps.expected: Registry identity, role, current application target and expected builds match.

steps.action: Save the attempt and verify a fresh identity proof using the existing server-verified public key.
steps.expected: The old firmware, identity, key and current boot match; a durable attempt is retained.

steps.action: Enter Heltec USB bootloader, refresh and explicitly confirm the identified device and image.
steps.expected: The selected hardware matches the preflight and the operator reviews the application update.

steps.action: Save the write intent, validate the image and install through the guarded firmware owner.
steps.expected: Only the qualified CORE application image is written; failure or interruption remains unresolved without automatic retry.

steps.action: Verify a fresh identity proof after boot and compare the registry ownership.
steps.expected: The same identity and public key return with the new source and a different boot; ownership remains unchanged.

steps.action: Review and retain the private update report.
steps.expected: The completed or incomplete attempt, proofs and installation evidence are retained locally.

limits: The bootloader USB identifier is not a cryptographic proof. Physical preservation and interrupted-write recovery require device evidence. No ownership, provisioning or credential area mutation is part of this procedure.
